title: Storage sections and sorting
summary: Storage in Supermarket Simulator is not one big cupboard: the game builds it out of sections and individually sortable cells, and the same section idea appears in growth.
body: Storage is made of sections rather than a single list, which is why putting something away is a choice of where rather than only what.
Cells inside that storage can be sorted, so the order you keep stock in is something the game lets you decide on purpose.
The same section idea is used elsewhere, including growth, which is why screens in this game tend to be organised the same way.
Sorting is kept as its own state. The game names a sort state and a sort result, which is the vocabulary behind a cell order rather than a fixed arrangement.
What this entry does not tell you: how many cells a shop has or how much each one holds. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Storage is built from sections rather than one flat list.
Growth is presented through the same section idea.
Sorting is kept as a state of its own with a result.
The build names a rack of its own, a material for it and an in-rack amount label.
facts.evidence: asset names: 7_SmallRack, M_Cloth_Rack, In Rack Amount

facts.claim: The storage section is an item of its own in the build, with a blueprint beside it.
facts.evidence: asset names: Storage Section Item, Storage Section ItemBP

facts.claim: The build names areas of its own as well: a crate area, a fill area, a slider area with its handle, and a text area.
facts.evidence: asset names: CrateArea, Fill Area, Sliding Area, Handle Slide Area, Text Area
